title: v0.27.1: live pipeline-parallel execution via torch.distributed.pipelining
body:
## Context

v0.27.0 ships `training.parallelism: pipeline` + `pipeline_stages: N` config fields + `utils/pipeline.validate_pipeline_config` validator, but the trainer does NOT actually execute pipelined forward/backward. When the validator passes, a Rich Panel notifies the user:

> Pipeline parallelism is configured (N stages) but live execution wiring ships in v0.27.1. Your config is validated and the trainer will run in data-parallel mode for now.

## Proposal for v0.27.1

Wire `torch.distributed.pipelining` (aka PiPPy / torch.pipelining) to partition the model across `pipeline_stages` devices with micro-batches:
1. On trainer setup, detect `cfg.training.parallelism == "pipeline"`
2. Use `torch.distributed.pipelining.pipeline(module, num_stages=N, example_args=...)` to partition
3. Replace the HF Trainer's forward with a pipeline-aware step
4. Micro-batch size auto-calculated as `batch_size // pipeline_stages`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Works for `base: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct` with `pipeline_stages: 4` on a 4xA100 node
- [ ] Automatic micro-batch split + accumulation
- [ ] Gradient accumulation remains correct across stages
- [ ] Recipe `deepseek-v3-pipeline` trains a smoke batch end-to-end
- [ ] Integration test that mocks `torch.distributed.pipelining` and verifies the partition call

## Proposed fix path

1. New `soup_cli/trainer/pipeline.py` — `PipelineTrainerWrapper` that subclasses the HF `Trainer` with a pipelined `training_step`
2. `commands/train.py` routes `cfg.training.parallelism == "pipeline"` to the new wrapper
3. Drop the Panel notice once execution lands

## Risk notes

- `torch.distributed.pipelining` is experimental in torch 2.3+; pin minimum
- Requires matching `accelerate launch --num_processes N` where N == pipeline_stages
- Checkpointing semantics change — `save_steps` may need adjustment

hey @MakazhanAlpamys 
would love to work on this

@AaronProbha18 — before I assign this, read the scope honestly, because it is one of the largest open items in the tracker and I would rather you choose it knowing that than discover it in week two.

**What it actually requires.** Acceptance criterion 1 is `Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct` with `pipeline_stages: 4` on a **4xA100 node**. Not a proxy, not a mock: pipeline parallelism is a distributed execution change, and a partitioned forward/backward that "looks right" on one GPU tells you almost nothing about whether gradient accumulation stayed correct across stages. Criterion 5 (a mocked partition call) is the only part a laptop can prove, and it is the least valuable of the five.

**So the first question is hardware.** Do you have multi-GPU access — owned, institutional, or a cloud budget you are willing to spend? If yes, say which and this is yours. If no, I would rather point you somewhere your work can be verified than have you write a large PR neither of us can accept.

**If you want it anyway with no hardware**, there is an honest version: land `soup_cli/trainer/pipeline.py` with the partition wiring and the mocked integration test, leave the Rich notice in place, and state plainly in the PR that criteria 1-4 are unverified. I would review it and probably merge it as a foundation, but I would not let it claim pipeline parallelism works, and the notice would stay until someone measures it. That is a real contribution; it is just a smaller one than the issue title promises.

**Alternatives sized for a first contribution here**, all currently unclaimed and all verifiable on one machine:

- **#783** — the path-containment scanner does not inspect `contextlib.suppress(ValueError)`. One node type, a clear acceptance list, and the surrounding test file shows you the pattern.
- **#780 (the guard half)** — a startup-budget test expressed as a ratio against the interpreter floor. Self-contained, and the measurement is already in the issue.
- **#761** — four documented config settings that do nothing. Pick one, prove it is ignored, wire or refuse it.

Tell me which way you want to go and I will assign it. No pressure toward the smaller ones if you have the GPUs — this issue has been open a long time precisely because nobody with the hardware has picked it up.

Hey, thanks for pointing that out! I don’t have access to the GPUs needed for this one, so I’ll go with something I can properly verify.

I’ll pick up **#783 — Path-containment ratchet does not inspect `contextlib.suppress(ValueError)`, which is already an idiom in this repo.**

Unassigning @AaronProbha18 — they declined this on 2026-09-11 ("I don't have access to the GPUs needed for this one") and took #783 instead, but the assignee field was never cleared. That is my bookkeeping error, and the cost is real: a large `help wanted` issue has been reading as taken for a week.

**This is open and unclaimed.** It needs multi-GPU hardware to validate, which is the reason it has sat — say so on the thread before starting so nobody duplicates the effort.

Adding `infra-blocked`: the acceptance criteria need a 4xA100 node (Llama-3.1-70B with `pipeline_stages: 4`), which cannot be verified in the local harness. It stays open and `help wanted` stays on for anyone with multi-GPU access; please comment here before starting.
